newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank securities unit in settlement.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank securities unit in settlement.

text.p: A Florida probe of sales practices in the securities business of NationsBank Corp. ended Tuesday, as the company agreed to an independent review of its activities and to pay $850,000 to the state.

According to a statement issued by Florida's Office of the Comptroller and by the state attorney general Tuesday, the NationSecurities unit also agreed to begin an arbitration process to make payments to investors.
The probe focused on issues of poor training and lack of supervision, a lawyer for the state said. The settlement said there was no finding that any law had been violated.

"We have moved forward from 1994 and we are glad to put this behind us," said NationsBank executive vice president John Munce in a telephone interview. He noted that the probe covered activities that occurred in 1993 and 1994.

"We believe that the spirit of the agreement which creates the education fund is consistent with our objective at all times, which is to to meet the financial needs of our customers," Munce said. The payment includes $250,000 to establish an investor education programme in Florida.

The agreement also provides that NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., will pay $300,000 to the Office of the Attorney General's Legal Affairs Revolving Trust Fund. Another $300,000 will go to the Department of Banking and Finance to cover legal fees and investigative costs.

"This settlement will provide greater oversight and consumer protection, while at the same time eliminating potentially lengthy legal proceedings," Florida Comptroller Robert Milligan said in a statement.
The agreement also sets a dispute resolution process to resolve customer complaints on file with the department and handle the payment of any claims resulting from the dispute.

The settlement also requires NationsSecurities to contract with an indepedent consultant to review broker-dealer compliance and to report to the comptroller within 120 days. The firm will maintain a ratio of at least one supervisor for every 25 brokers selling investments.
Shares of NationsBank, the nation's fourth-largest banking company, rose 75 cents to $60.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
